title: us-evolution-education-lpm Institutional Mandate Record
description: A single named, dated commitment that binds ALL US states at once -- the one level above florida-lpm's/pennsylvania-lpm's/tennessee-lpm's own state- or district-level mandates. The computable unit for 'what does this authority actually require', so a coherence-finding record can point at exactly which mandate it tests. Modeled on deutsche_lp's/nys_lp's/india-lpm's/florida-lpm's/pennsylvania-lpm's/tennessee-lpm's institutional-mandate-record.schema.json; mandateType adds 'federal-supreme-court-precedent', the one new schema mechanism this repo contributes back -- none of the three state repos needed it, since none of the rulings they document bound more than one state (florida-lpm, tennessee-lpm) or one federal circuit (pennsylvania-lpm's Kitzmiller is a single federal DISTRICT ruling, binding only that district, however nationally influential).

jurisdiction.description: Almost always bare 'US' in this repo, since its whole purpose is mandates that bind every state at once -- a state-specific code would belong in that state's own repo instead.

issuingBody.description: Free text, e.g. 'Supreme Court of the United States'. Not a controlled vocabulary.

mandateType.description: The first six values are inherited unchanged from the sibling repos and not expected to be used here (this repo's own mandates are all national in scope). 'federal-supreme-court-precedent' = a binding requirement set by a US Supreme Court ruling rather than a statute or board vote -- e.g. Epperson v. Arkansas (1968) and Edwards v. Aguillard (1987), both of which establish what NO state may require, binding all fifty states at once. Distinct from a lower federal court's ruling (a single district or circuit, which binds only that district/circuit and belongs in the relevant state repo instead -- see pennsylvania-lpm's Kitzmiller v. Dover, a federal DISTRICT ruling, and tennessee-lpm's Daniel v. Waters, a federal CIRCUIT ruling, neither of which is national in binding scope even though both are nationally influential).

interdisciplinaryExplicitness.description: Optional, kept for structural parity with deutsche_lp/nys_lp's identical field -- whether this mandate's own text uses interdisciplinary/cross-subject framing. Expected to be 'silent-on-cross-subject' or 'unspecified' for every mandate in this repo, since a Supreme Court ruling is not a benchmark list.

statementText.description: The mandate's own text, quoted exactly (or as exactly as the available source allows) as read in the primary source -- e.g. a Supreme Court opinion's own holding language. Do not paraphrase where a verbatim quote is available.

targetDate.description: If the mandate names a completion/implementation horizon distinct from its adoption date (e.g. 'full implementation begins school year 2027-28' for a prospective 2026 readoption).

status.description: 'adopted' = formally in force (a completed State Board regulatory rulemaking, a signed statute, an enacted school-district board policy). 'proposed' = drafted/released for public comment or introduced but not yet binding. 'superseded' = replaced by a later mandate (link via supersededBy).

accessTier.description: How much of the underlying mandate document this record actually keeps, chosen per-source based on what's legally safe to redistribute for this document -- not one all-or-nothing repo-wide rule. Governs statementText specifically. 'full-text-stored' = statementText reproduces the mandate's full relevant text -- the de facto tier this repo uses, since a US Supreme Court opinion is a public judicial record with no copyright restriction at all. 'excerpt-only' = statementText is a short, bounded quotation. 'summary-only' = statementText is paraphrase only. 'citation-only' = no statementText at all. Identical field to deutsche_lp's/nys_lp's/india-lpm's/florida-lpm's/pennsylvania-lpm's/tennessee-lpm's institutional-mandate-record.schema.json.

licenseOrRightsNote.description: The legal basis for storing this mandate's statementText at the accessTier chosen above -- for every mandate in this repo, 'a US Supreme Court opinion is a public judicial record, not subject to copyright.' Mirrors OpenLPM's standards_documents.license_or_rights_note field (openlpm migration 019) for ecosystem-wide naming consistency.
